philosophy.title: How I think about design
philosophy.lead: I want to create products that are solutions for problems worth solving.
body: I'm interested in the psychology of design — principles like MAYA, and how bias shapes whether people accept a design — and in what layout, composition and typography communicate before anything is read.

I lean toward a life-centred approach rather than a purely human-centred one, and toward considered detail rather than stripped-back minimalism. Less is not always more. Sustainability, to me, means longevity: objects that last and can be repaired with replaceable components.

strengths.title: Making and modelling
strengths.body: Clay, foam, card and cardboard prototypes used as thinking tools, alongside workshop skills including lathe turning, carving and finishing.

strengths.title: Drawing and communication
strengths.body: Ideation sketching, orthographic and manufacturing drawings, rendering, and presentation pages that explain how an object works.

strengths.title: Fine art
strengths.body: Watercolour, acrylics, alcohol marker and tonal pencil work, plus graphics and illustration produced for competition and enterprise projects.

strengths.title: Curiosity and empathy
strengths.body: I'm curious about how things work and why the designer made the choices they did, and empathic enough to want to understand the user's emotions, needs and problems.

contact.title: Get in touch
contact.lead: Happy to talk about design work, projects or making. Email is the quickest way to reach me.
